Stochastic Tree Ensemble Bayesian Causal Forest Regression Learner

Source: R/learner_stochtree_regr_stochtree_bcf.R
mlr_learners_regr.stochtree_bcf.Rd

Bayesian causal forest (BCF) sampled with MCMC, optionally warm-started with the grow-from-root algorithm of accelerated BCF (XBCF). Calls stochtree::bcf() from stochtree.

The model decomposes the outcome into a prognostic forest and a treatment effect forest, i.e., y = mu(x) + tau(x) * z, where z is the treatment. As mlr3 has no task type for causal inference, the treatment is a feature of the regression task that is selected with the treatment parameter. The learner predicts the outcome given the covariates and the observed treatment, so resampling and tuning evaluate the outcome prediction and not the treatment effect. The estimated conditional average treatment effect is returned by the $treatment_effect() method.

The "se" predict type returns the posterior standard deviation of the conditional mean. Propensity scores are estimated internally by stochtree::bcf(). Random effects are not supported.

Custom mlr3 parameters

  • treatment: Name of the feature that contains the treatment. The feature must be logical, integer, or numeric, and is passed as Z_train to stochtree::bcf(). All other features are used as covariates. This parameter is required.

  • stochtree::bcf() takes most of its parameters in the lists general_params, prognostic_forest_params, treatment_effect_forest_params, and variance_forest_params. The entries of these lists are exposed as individual hyperparameters. The entries of general_params keep their names. The entries of the forest lists that occur in more than one list are prefixed with prognostic_, treatment_, and variance_, e.g., prognostic_num_trees, treatment_num_trees, and variance_num_trees. All other entries of the forest lists keep their names.

  • random_seed: If not set, the seed of the C++ random number generator is drawn from R's random number generator. Upstream seeds from std::random_device in this case.

Reproducibility

stochtree::bcf() estimates the propensity scores with an internal BART model that is always seeded from std::random_device. Results are therefore only reproducible with set.seed() or random_seed when propensity_covariate is "none", in which case no propensity model is fitted.

  • observation_weights is not exposed as a hyperparameter. Observation weights are taken from the task instead, see the weights property.

Dictionary

This Learner can be instantiated via lrn():

lrn("regr.stochtree_bcf")

Saving a Learner

The fitted model holds pointers to C++ objects. In order to save a trained learner, or to use it with encapsulation or parallelization, the model is marshaled to a JSON string with stochtree::saveBARTModelToJsonString(). Call $marshal() before saving the learner with saveRDS() and $unmarshal() after reading it.

Herren, Drew, Hahn, Richard, Murray, Jared, Carvalho, Carlos, He, Jingyu (2026). stochtree: Stochastic Tree Ensembles (XBART and BART) for Supervised Learning and Causal Inference. doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.stochtree . R package version 0.4.5.

Examples

# Define the Learner, the treatment is a feature of the task
learner = lrn("regr.stochtree_bcf", treatment = "am")
print(learner)
#> 
#> ── <LearnerRegrStochtreeBCF> (regr.stochtree_bcf): Stochastic Tree Ensemble Baye
#> • Model: -
#> • Parameters: treatment=am
#> • Packages: mlr3, mlr3extralearners, and stochtree
#> • Predict Types: [response] and se
#> • Feature Types: logical, integer, numeric, factor, and ordered
#> • Encapsulation: none (fallback: -)
#> • Properties: marshal and weights
#> • Other settings: use_weights = 'use', predict_raw = 'FALSE'

# Define a Task
task = tsk("mtcars")

# Create train and test set
ids = partition(task)

# Train the learner on the training ids
learner$train(task, row_ids = ids$train)

# Make predictions of the outcome for the test rows
predictions = learner$predict(task, row_ids = ids$test)

# Score the predictions
predictions$score()
#> regr.mse 
#> 7.270069 

# Estimate the conditional average treatment effect for the test rows
learner$treatment_effect(task, row_ids = ids$test)
#>  [1] 3.434679 3.034534 4.519530 4.119840 3.227515 3.232026 3.094623 3.074822
#>  [9] 4.567235 3.224447 4.425102
